name: Aristides Pereira International Airport
before:
The airport for Boa Vista in Cape Verde, about 5 km south east of the island capital Sal Rei, and third busiest in the country.

It became an international airport fairly recently. The existing Rabil airfield was converted between 2005 and 2007, with the runway extended from 1,200 to 2,100 metres and widened from 30 to 45 metres at a cost of 21 million euros. It opened officially on 31 October 2007, which is what made Boa Vista's package holiday market possible.

Ownership changed in July 2023, when Vinci Airports finalised a 40-year concession covering seven Cape Verde airports, alongside ANA-Aeroportos de Portugal which holds 30 per cent. Vinci is responsible for funding, operating and expanding them, so facilities here should improve over the concession.
after:
The airport for Boa Vista in Cape Verde, and the third busiest in the country.

It became an international airport in 2007, when the old Rabil airfield was converted. Its runway is 2,100 metres long and 45 metres wide.

Since July 2023 it has been run by Cabo Verde Airports, 70 per cent owned by Vinci Airports and 30 per cent by ANA-Aeroportos de Portugal, under a 40-year concession covering seven Cape Verde airports. Vinci is responsible for funding, operating and expanding them, so facilities here should improve over the concession.

claims.claim: opened officially on 31 October 2007; made the package holiday market possible
claims.wasBefore: It opened officially on 31 October 2007, which is what made Boa Vista's package holiday market possible.
claims.why: The day rests on Wikipedia alone (the operator gives only the year, kept). The package holiday claim is in no source, Wikipedia included: an inference. The operator says the island is one of the most tourist-oriented in Cape Verde and the airport the way in for many foreign tourists, but only on its own pages.

claims.wasBefore: Ownership changed in July 2023, when Vinci Airports finalised a 40-year concession covering seven Cape Verde airports, alongside ANA-Aeroportos de Portugal which holds 30 per cent.
claims.why: Wrong in kind: a 40-year concession, not a change of ownership. Rewritten with the operator's own terms (see above).

claims.claim: FCDO: pre-register and pay the TSA 5 days ahead (double at the border from 1 July 2026); blue and yellow authorised taxis; sandstorms disrupt Boa Vista flights
claims.why: Held back: advice that replaces nothing in the old text. The FCDO (updated 28 July 2026, still current 24 September 2026) says visitors must pre-register and pay the airport security fee (TSA) online at least 5 days before arrival, and from 1 July 2026 pay double at the border without proof; British visitors need no visa for up to 30 days; authorised taxis on Sal and Boa Vista are blue and yellow; and sandstorms ('bruma seca') between December and February can disrupt air travel, especially on Boa Vista. SID's Overview carries the first two (added before the held-back rule). For Andy to decide.
